title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 46
paragraphs: Now the region of the Euxine against which Darius was preparing to march contains, apart from the Scythian race, the most ignorant nations of all lands; for we can point to no people in the region of the Pontus distinguished for ability, nor do we know of any learned man who has arisen there, apart from the Scythian nation and Anacharsis. By the Scythians, one thing—the most important of all human matters—has been discovered more cleverly than by any other men we know; in other respects, I have no great admiration for them. That most important thing they have discovered is such that no one who has come to attack them can escape again; and if they do not wish to be found, it is impossible to catch them. For they who have no cities founded, no walls built, but carry their houses with them and are mounted archers, living not from the plough but from cattle, and whose dwellings are upon wagons—these are surely invincible and impossible to approach.
